ov: Simple animals fixed to the seabed, with bodies full of pores and channels. They have no true tissues, organs or nerves: beating cells pull water through the body and filter out tiny food. Most live in the sea, but some live in fresh water.
rg: Seas worldwide, from the tide zone to more than 8,800 m deep; freshwater sponges live on every continent except Antarctica.
df: Bacteria-sized particles and other tiny food filtered from the water it pumps through its body.
fx: Some sponges can rebuild their whole body from cells that have been separated from each other.
Their skeletons were the original bath and cleaning sponges, though few are used that way now.
